{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZsxKIA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDTC90", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 133, "title": "Grow the local PC-VAN community to 100 diverse residents and improve timely OLT/forum responses", "body": "## Problem

The PC-VAN local world currently has **ten fictional resident profiles**. Their credible individual routines and interests make the world feel authentic, but this small population often leaves OLT rooms empty and causes long stretches without any response to a human's forum post. The user wants a more lively yet believable 1996–1997-style community, **not** an artificial rule that guarantees an instant reply or forces someone into every room.

A population around **100 distinct residents**, with *genuinely varied* login habits, schedule coverage, topics and friendships, should naturally improve the odds that an interested resident is active whenever someone visits: nearly-always-present regulars, long-stay night owls, early risers, daytime/shift workers, students, weekend-only users, quiet lurkers, intermittently absent members and people with unusual schedules. At the same time, OLT and forum response selection must actually prioritize **present, relevant** people on human interaction. Increasing headcount without changing the current response selection/rate limits will not solve the UX problem.

Do **not** make every resident run a model independently. Resident *identity, profile, presence and eligibility* should be cheap; only a small number of actual authored speech/post turns should invoke the already consented local WebLLM.

## Expected outcome

### 1. A coherent community of approximately 100 distinct residents

- Expand from the current **10 to around 100 stable fictional residents** in a newly initialized or factory-reset world. Preserve the original ten IDs, names, characters and existing seed post authors.
- Give each added member an original Japanese handle, believable occupation/life situation, distinct voice and interests, preferred boards/SIGs, weekly/daily routines, likelihood of being away, reply/reading/posting habits and a **sparse, meaningful** network of affinities. Avoid 90 generic copies of a template or names alone with no behavioral variation; write original fictional profiles rather than borrowing real historical members.
- Include a *small minority* of very frequent / long-stay participants (even somebody who tends to be connected across much of the day, sometimes absent), recurring night/early-morning/daytime users, weekday/weekend-specific users and sporadic/mostly-reading people. Do not force one permanently logged-in character into every room or deterministic constant headcounts.
- Preserve the distinction between the cheap roster (100 members), smaller currently present/active subset, and **far fewer model-generated turns**. Do not introduce a server, remote users, permanent background processing or 100 concurrent WebLLM instances.

### 2. An OLT that is pleasant to enter at different hours

- Distribute resident presence over **all 24 local JST hours**, weekday and weekend, without the same people being present all the time. Different rooms and hours may have one, several or occasionally no attendees; in normal sampled visits it should usually be possible to encounter someone or see an arrival soon after joining.
- Use overlapping individual routines, individual participation/absence probabilities, realistic session lengths, favored rooms/SIGs and a few long-stay habitual visitors. On entering OLT, membership and attendance should reflect current simulated presence **promptly**, rather than requiring a long real-time wait for the first visitor. People may independently join/leave during a session; preserve identity and continuity across observations/re-entry.
- When an authorized model is ready and a human speaks, select an **actually present** resident with topical interest and/or relevant affinity. Start a plausible, fairly prompt reply opportunity (rough target **tens of seconds**, not minutes, excluding model loading/inference time) when someone suitable is there; allow silence, failed inference and intermittent empty rooms. The model generation and UI must remain responsive and never steal IME/input focus.
- Keep occasional spontaneous resident-to-resident small talk and arrivals, without flooding the terminal or requiring a human to initiate every line. Never label scripted/presence activity as AI-generated dialogue. If no model was authorized, human speech and readback still work, but do not fabricate model responses.

### 3. Forum replies that are timely *because someone suitable is around*

- Human-created forum threads/replies should create an **eligible near-term attention opportunity** for one or a few interested residents whose routines make them available, rather than being lost among hundreds of random scheduled activities. A fitting resident's response can happen within a few minutes (design target around **1–3 minutes** when the tab is visible and the already-loaded model is available), without requiring a manual GENERATE/PREVIEW/SEND action.
- The existing **20-minute minimum age for reply candidates** and coarse hourly/random opportunity selection in `src/ai/activity.ts` must be reconsidered for human-triggered replies. Keep slower organic activity (new threads and AI-to-AI continuation) and genuine quiet periods; don't guarantee that every post gets a reply or let one human monopolize the population.
- Use forum topic, resident expertise, active-time overlap, public thread context, existing relationships and fairness/repetition limits to choose *who* answers. The same named person who appears in a forum can appear in OLT/mail, with stable memory/identity. Do not leak private mail content into public posts/OLT.

### 4. Bound cost independently from roster size

- Keep inference local, **explicitly opt-in**, with one shared WebLLM adapter/worker and cross-tab lease; no background inference when the browser is closed or hidden, no extra downloads or automatic model authorization.
- Cap actual model generations, pending work, event history and time spent considering candidates, **independently of whether the world has 10, 100, or eventually 1000 identities**. Avoid O(residents × all posts × all rooms) repeated scans where bounded candidate preselection/indexing is sufficient.
- Review existing conservative caps (`maxPosts` default four per six hours, `MAX_SESSION_POSTS` 12, separate OLT 24 attempts/hour) and prevent them from starving visible human-facing responses or forum activity. If a dedicated user-response budget/priority is warranted, make it small, bounded, restart-safe and fair; do not silently convert 100 members into 100 simultaneous generation jobs or unlimited posting.
- Keep prompt windows small and scoped: selected person's profile, bounded relevant public context and OLT participants, rather than injecting 100 full biographies, social graphs or the entire forum archive into every model call.

### 5. Preserve the product's immersive interaction boundary

- Everything *within PC-VAN* remains terminal-keyboard-only: SIG navigation, forum WRITE/REPLY, OLT JOIN/WHO/speech/LEAVE and mail. Modern AI setup, resident management, reset/backup and technical provenance stay in the existing **設定 / Options** dialog. Adapt the current ten-resident Settings editor for a larger roster with usable navigation/filtering, not a giant unbounded list that disrupts ordinary play.
- Ordinary terminal text should show handles, departures, topics and messages, not model status, generation buttons or authenticity disclaimers. The work is a **fictional local reconstruction**, not a claim to authenticate real 1996–1997 people or commands.
- Follow the user's prior scope preference: prioritize **new/factory-reset worlds**. No requirement to backfill 90 new characters into old or imported worlds through a complex migration wizard. The existing explicit reset is an acceptable route to the refreshed baseline. Still honor and validate any legacy/imported records you actually support, avoid crashing on open, and never overwrite user-created posts or re-create deliberately removed records on ordinary reload.

## Context

Baseline checked for this Issue: `main` at `4e05eddb0298aa9bc4cc0be33f7d617807d835d2` (merge of #131). Confirm current head before implementation.

Current code illustrates why this is a **behavior + scalability** issue, not a roster-only fixture change:

- `src/ai/personas.ts`: hardcoded array of ten `personas`, `ResidentSettings.version === 1`, routines, preferred boards and affinities; `personaMemberId()` supplies stable IDs shared across services.
- `src/storage/schema.ts`: `validateResidents` explicitly requires `profiles.length === 10`, and `validateActivity` checks scheduled run persona IDs against the original constant list. OLT reserved-state validation also enforces ten present residents. Any new member/profile approach must update every cardinality assumption, serialized settings, backup/restore validation, presence references and editing.
- `src/ai/activity.ts`: per-person opportunity loops, full forum/post filtering and preference scoring, `>=20 minutes` parent age, six-hour bounded run allowances and slow due cadence. `initialDue` draws from the constant `personas`, so scheduling must include new members.
- `src/olt-state.ts`: 20-minute seeded windows, 7–18-minute stays, rare attendance based on routine and per-member visit selection, maximum ten resident presences and bounded room transcript. `src/ai/olt.ts` only picks from present candidates, silences are legitimate, and it enforces 24 model attempts/hour across rooms. Room context separation (DAISIZEN vs Wakaba), two-tab leases, expiry and timeouts must remain intact.
- `src/ai/controls.ts`, `src/ai/olt.ts`, `src/ai/mail.ts` and `src/storage/repository.ts` share consent/worker, local identity, scheduled mail/forum actions, atomic persistence and stale-world protection. Avoid a second model worker or bypassing model consent just to achieve prompt responses.
- `docs/local-ai.md`, `docs/sig-navigation.md`, `tests/activity.spec.ts`, `tests/autonomy.spec.ts`, `tests/olt.spec.ts`, `tests/olt-repository.spec.ts`, `tests/residents.spec.ts`, `tests/mail-autonomy.spec.ts`, `tests/factory-reset.spec.ts` and Settings tests define current expectations.
- #51 (expanded SIGs), #52 (mail), #53 (OLT), #131 (all new-world public boards populated) have already been implemented. Maintain consistent identities and authorship across those services.
- Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md). English Issue/PR/docs and Japanese UI text.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] **New and confirmed-reset worlds have approximately 100 original fictional resident member IDs/profiles** (target 100), including the original 10 unchanged identities and seed-author links; no duplicate handles/IDs or accidental renaming/rewriting of old posts. Profiles have varied credible occupations, daytime/nighttime/weekend patterns, interests, voices, affiliations, participation/absence and sparse affinities, rather than randomized superficial clones.
- [ ] Replace ten-specific assumptions in profile validation, activity IDs, initial due scheduling, local settings/backup, mail addressing/identity, OLT presence/turn validation and resident editor. New-world persistence/reload/JSON backup/import/reset and cross-tab behavior work without creating extra people or breaking references. **No elaborate compatibility/backfill UI for existing local worlds** is required.
- [ ] Add **deterministic simulated-week sampling** (weekday, weekend, each JST hour and multiple seeds) showing recognizable differences in who is present and which rooms are busy/quiet, with meaningful day/night diversity. Document plausible qualitative or quantitative acceptance thresholds *based on this design*; avoid fixing everyone online and avoid an unconditional “always 1–2 people in every room” special case. Verify that a freshly entered typical room often has someone or gets a natural arrival promptly.
- [ ] With mock authorized inference and controlled time, simulate human OLT speech at representative early-morning/day/evening/night slots. When a relevant resident is present and eligible, a possible response is planned **within tens of seconds**, respects model readiness/actual inference time and does not require explicit AI-generation commands. Test legitimate silence/absence, AI-to-AI turns, rate limiting, attendance lease, hide/leave cancellation, focus/IME and repeat visits; no fake replies without model consent.
- [ ] A human forum WRITE/REPLY receives prompt, interest-appropriate *opportunities* (rough target **1–3 minutes under a visible tab with a warm, consented mock model**), without a universal promise to answer. Cover a fitting active resident, sleeping/absent specialists, busy model and exhausted quota; do not force unrelated users to answer or remove organic longer-delayed discussions. Human and resident posts persist with correct parent IDs and no duplicate/late commits.
- [ ] No model weights download or worker spawn is triggered by merely starting/opening a 100-resident world; measuring roster/presence/scheduling alone does not invoke the model. Keep model concurrency at **one shared authorized worker**, bounded prompts, OLT and forum/mail budgets, bounded chronological catch-up, stale-world fences and browser-only no-closed-tab behavior.
- [ ] Benchmark deterministic profiling/planning, OLT observation, normal terminal navigation and world bootstrap at **10 vs 100 profiles** (and, if useful, synthetic **1000-profile performance-only** input). Document actual execution/runtime/memory observations in the same environment; establish reasonable bounds rather than claiming 1000 is free or requiring full 1000 resident content now. Eliminate obvious quadratic repeated scans and avoid unnecessarily increasing database/terminal work.
- [ ] Keep all currently populated boards (#131), original and new posts, shared forum/mail/OLT identities, mail and OLT privacy boundaries, historical timeline projection, Settings separation, user handle selection and backup/reset behavior. Imported/old/custom worlds must not be silently repopulated or corrupted merely by opening a newer version.
- [ ] Add/adjust focused deterministic unit, real IndexedDB, browser and mocked-WebLLM tests covering roster uniqueness/character diversity, 24-hour and weekly presence distributions, user-directed response timing, fair silence, quotas, multi-tab duplicate prevention, reload/restore/reset, local consent and Japanese IME. Avoid multiplying the suite with hundreds of near-identical per-person tests; use data-level invariants and representative journeys.
- [ ] Update README, local-AI/OLT/SIG documentation, sources/provenance limitations and any help/settings copy that assumes exactly ten. Run `npm test` and `npm run build` and accurately report results, failures and skipped optional tests.

## Optional validation

Human exploration of several open OLT sessions at different simulated hours and forum topics, plus a real WebGPU/model trial to assess actual generation latency and Japanese persona quality. Optional performance checks on lower-end hardware. These are useful but should not block deterministic/mock acceptance in CI.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Production-asset browser checks and mocks can validate the release before merge; deployment follows the repository's normal GitHub Pages flow.
